steps.page: Sample walkthrough 1 of 4: what you asked for, and what you got
steps.intro: A real walkthrough of the deck changes built so far, in the proposed format. Every row stands unless you press Change this or More context. Drag on any picture.

steps.path: Any deck link I send you
steps.headline: What you asked for, and what you got

calls.call: Drag a rectangle on any picture to comment on that area.
calls.why: A numbered box opens under the picture. The rectangle and your words are saved together.
calls.decided: "rectangular drag-regions instead of single-dot pins … highlight any size rectangle within an image and comment on it"

calls.call: Lists where every row stands unless you flag it, each with its own text box.
calls.why: Used for calls I made, and for every page of this walkthrough. Also shows the microphone while listening.
calls.decided: "each item i choose to change should have its own little text box underneath/attached to it"

calls.call: The deck shows when it was built and from which version; each answer shows its time.
calls.why: Top-left label on every page, and an Answered column on the finish screen.
calls.decided: "tracking the date/time and branch/commit a deck was built against, specific date/time each question is answered by me"

calls.call: A small (i) beside "Today" says how and when I checked that fact.
calls.why: Hover it. It is visible in the first picture above.
calls.decided: "can just be hidden behind a little (i) hover popup next to the today section header"

calls.call: A microphone in every text box, using the same speech model as YouCoded.
calls.why: Press, speak, press again. A ring grows with your voice.
calls.decided: "I want to be able to respond to these decks with my voice"

calls.call: A question answered by typing has no second note box.
calls.why: It was a one-line cause.
calls.decided: "there should never be two text fields in an answer"

calls.call: The big green circle no longer appears on an answered question.
calls.why: The finish-screen circle style was leaking onto the word "answered".
calls.decided: "weird green answered circle … distorts the card"

calls.call: "Don't know" is now "Other" on yes/no questions.
calls.why: One button, same meaning. A typed-answer question has no extra button at all.
calls.decided: "i think this should also just be other"

calls.call: A "More context" button on every list row.
calls.why: A row you cannot judge yet is flagged for me to explain next round, instead of counting as accepted.
calls.decided: "something like your additional context button could be useful"

steps.page: Sample walkthrough 2 of 4: behind the scenes
steps.intro: What happens when you use it, in order, for the parts with no screen of their own.

steps.path: Any deck link I send you
steps.headline: What happens when you speak an answer, and when you submit

calls.call: You press the microphone. The page asks the deck's own small helper to start listening.
calls.why: The app refuses the microphone to any page shown inside it, so the page cannot listen by itself.

calls.call: The helper records from this computer's microphone and runs the speech files YouCoded already downloaded.
calls.why: Nothing new is downloaded and the running app is never contacted.

calls.call: About once a second it listens to the whole recording again and sends the words so far to the box.
calls.why: Listening again from the start lets later words correct earlier ones. The app does the same.

calls.call: You press again. It makes one last pass, stops, and the words stay in the box.
calls.why: There is no automatic stop on silence. A recording left running stops after five minutes.

calls.call: Every answer, area and flagged row is written to a file beside the deck within a third of a second.
calls.why: A crash or closed tab loses nothing already entered.

calls.call: You submit. The deck stops, and the chat reads that file, including each rectangle's position.
calls.why: The chat is told the moment the deck stops; nothing to copy or paste.

steps.page: Sample walkthrough 3 of 4: calls I made
steps.intro: Visible choices I made without asking, since round 2.

steps.path: Any deck link I send you
steps.headline: Calls I made for you

calls.call: Your rectangles are drawn in blue.
calls.why: The amber box on screenshots already means "this is what changed". Yours needed a different colour.

calls.call: A drag smaller than one hundredth of the picture is ignored.
calls.why: It is almost always a shaky click.

calls.call: "All fine" is switched off while any row is flagged.
calls.why: A yes that contradicts a flagged row was a real fault in past decks.

calls.call: The "Listening" line under the box is gone; the state shows when you hover the microphone.
calls.why: That line was the most likely cause of the box changing shape.

calls.call: Voice does not use your custom word list yet.
calls.why: The deck's helper is separate from the app. "YouCoded" may be misspelled.

calls.call: A row's two buttons sit side by side, and a row's picture sits to its left.
calls.why: Keeps rows short.

calls.call: All 353 automatic checks of the deck tool.
calls.why: Run after the last change today.

calls.why: This is now a permanent automatic check.

calls.why: You used both in round 2 and your areas and changes arrived with their positions.

steps.intro: You asked what each page is, how it earns its place, and what to merge or drop.

steps.path: Any deck link I send you
steps.headline: The pages of a walkthrough, and why each is there

calls.call: Page 1, What you asked for and what you got: one row per request, with your own words, a picture where there is a screen, and what it does.
calls.why: Merges two of my six parts (purpose, screens). It is the checklist for the finish line: every change you asked for must be a row.

calls.call: Page 2, Behind the scenes: numbered plain steps.
calls.why: The only place you see logic that has no screen, and how parts connect.

calls.call: Page 3, Calls I made.
calls.why: Nothing visible gets decided silently.

calls.call: Page 4, Checks, ending with what is left for you to verify.
calls.why: "Left for you" was too short for its own page, so it closes this one.

calls.call: Moving around uses the deck's normal page bar, one page per part. The row of chips in my drawing is dropped.
calls.why: You found chips plus pages confusing.

calls.call: Before building, the same four pages appear with drawings instead of screenshots, and suggested checks instead of results.
calls.why: Same shape both times, so the second read is quick.

steps.path: Any deck link I send you
steps.headline: Who decides what, revised from your note

calls.call: ASKED as a question: core user flows. The steps a person takes to get something done, and their order.
calls.why: You named this.

calls.call: ASKED: big-picture interface design. Which screens exist, what sits where, how a new control looks.
calls.why: You named this.

calls.call: ASKED: how features and parts of the app affect each other.
calls.why: You named this.

calls.call: ASKED: anything that removes or changes what an existing control does, or touches money or privacy.
calls.why: These are the surprises that cost trust.

calls.call: LISTED with my default, yours to overrule: wording on menus, buttons and messages.
calls.why: You suggested this move.

calls.call: LISTED: what happens when something fails.
calls.why: You suggested this move.

calls.call: LISTED: defaults, limits, sizes, spacing, and which existing style is reused.
calls.why: One obvious answer from the design guide.

calls.call: NEVER SHOWN: only what you could not detect by using the app in any way. File names, how the code is organised, test code.
calls.why: If it changes speed, storage, battery, cost, or what leaves the computer, it is not in this group; it is listed.

calls.call: When unsure between asked and listed: listed.
calls.why: Your answer to R-5.

calls.call: Asked items come in the first questions round. Listed items come in the walkthrough.
calls.why: You wanted the big questions during initial design.

steps.path: Any deck link I send you
steps.headline: Should decks get a page where you edit on-screen wording directly?
steps.today: Wording is asked as pick-one options or a single typed answer. Only the website has an edit-in-place tool.
steps.problem: For a menu with ten labels, that is ten questions, or my defaults with no easy way to fix one.
steps.proposal: A deck item that lists each piece of wording in its own editable box, filled with my default and labelled with where it appears. Retype any; untouched ones stand.

options.label: Editable boxes, labelled by where they appear
pros: Fits the lists you already use.
cons: You see the words in a list, not on the screen itself.

options.label: Edit directly on a live copy of the screen
pros: You see every word where it will sit.
cons: Much more to build, and only works once the screen exists.

steps.headline: Ready-made starting points for questions about looks

calls.call: Before and after of one change: two pictures side by side, yes or no.
calls.why: Exists today; gets clearer instructions.

calls.call: A fan of alternatives for one thing: three or four designs side by side, pick one.
calls.why: Exists today as the "choice" slide; underused.

calls.call: One new screen with nothing before it: one picture, build it or not.
calls.why: Exists today.

calls.call: A flow: several screens in the order a person meets them, each open to rectangles.
calls.why: New. Today a flow gets split into unrelated slides.

calls.call: Wording in place: the editable boxes from the question above.
calls.why: New, if you approve it.

calls.call: Instructions will say which of these to use when, with one filled-in example each.
calls.why: You asked for better templates and clearer instructions.

steps.path: Any deck link I send you
steps.headline: In a deck that grows over rounds, how should pages be grouped?
steps.today: Not built yet. You picked "new first, settled folded below" and asked for more thought on grouping.
steps.problem: If new questions all jump to one page, they lose their topic. If they stay in topic pages, you hunt for them.
steps.proposal: Pages keep their topic names across rounds. A page with anything new is marked in the page bar and opens first. Inside a page, new rows sit on top and settled ones fold below with your answer shown.

options.label: Keep topic pages; mark and open the ones with something new
pros: A new question keeps its context.
Pages do not get renamed or reshuffled.
cons: New items can be spread over several pages.

options.label: One "New this round" page first, then the topic pages
pros: Everything new is in one place.
cons: A new question sits apart from the settled ones it relates to.
